facts.claim: Abraham Lincoln was born in a one-room Kentucky log cabin
facts.context: Born February 12, 1809 near Hodgenville, Kentucky, to a farming family of very modest means.
facts.goDeeper: He was born the same day as Charles Darwin, on opposite sides of the Atlantic.

facts.claim: Abraham Lincoln's height
facts.context: Six feet four inches, which still makes him the tallest president in American history.
facts.goDeeper: He was strikingly thin with it, and contemporaries often described him as gaunt rather than imposing.

facts.claim: Lincoln and Stephen Douglas held their famous series of debates
facts.context: Seven debates across Illinois during the 1858 Senate campaign, each running about three hours.
facts.goDeeper: Lincoln lost that Senate race. The debates made him a national figure anyway, and won him the presidency two years later.

facts.claim: Number of Lincoln-Douglas debates
facts.context: Seven, one in each Illinois congressional district where the two had not already both spoken.
facts.goDeeper: There were no microphones. Both men had to project to crowds of thousands outdoors.

facts.claim: Lincoln began his single term in the United States House of Representatives
facts.context: He served one two-year term as a Whig congressman from Illinois and did not seek re-election.
facts.goDeeper: He opposed the Mexican-American War from the House floor, which was unpopular enough at home to help end that career.

facts.claim: Lincoln's age when he became president
facts.context: He turned 52 a few weeks before his inauguration in March 1861.
facts.goDeeper: Photographs taken four years apart show the toll the war took; he looks decades older by 1865.

facts.claim: Number of sons born to Abraham and Mary Lincoln
facts.context: Robert, Edward, William and Thomas. Only Robert lived to adulthood.
facts.goDeeper: Willie died in the White House in 1862, in the middle of the war. Mary never really recovered.

facts.claim: Lincoln was granted a patent for a device to lift boats over shoals
facts.context: Patent No. 6469, for inflatable bellows to buoy a vessel over sandbars. It was never manufactured.
facts.goDeeper: He remains the only American president to hold a patent.

facts.claim: Lincoln grew his beard after a letter from an eleven-year-old girl
facts.context: Grace Bedell wrote in October 1860 suggesting whiskers would improve his chances. He had grown them by the inauguration.
facts.goDeeper: He met her in person a few months later, at a train stop in New York, and told her he had taken her advice.

facts.claim: Lincoln delivered his second inaugural address
facts.context: March 4, 1865, six weeks before his death. It ends 'with malice toward none, with charity for all'.
facts.goDeeper: It runs to just 701 words, and much of it is about forgiveness rather than victory.

facts.claim: Lincoln gave the 'house divided against itself cannot stand' speech
facts.context: Delivered in Springfield in June 1858 on accepting the Republican nomination for the Senate.
facts.goDeeper: Advisers told him the line was too radical and would cost him the election. He used it anyway.

facts.claim: The Lincoln Memorial in Washington was dedicated
facts.context: Dedicated May 30, 1922, fifty-seven years after his death.
facts.goDeeper: The dedication ceremony itself was segregated, with Black attendees seated in a separate section.

facts.claim: Height of the seated Lincoln statue inside the Lincoln Memorial
facts.context: The marble figure is about 19 feet tall. Standing, the figure would be roughly 28 feet.
facts.goDeeper: It was carved from 28 separate blocks of Georgia marble and assembled inside the building.

facts.claim: Lincoln first appeared on the American one-cent coin
facts.context: Introduced for the centenary of his birth, replacing the Indian Head cent.
facts.goDeeper: He was the first real person to appear on a circulating US coin; before that the designs were allegorical figures.

facts.claim: Lincoln's annual salary as president
facts.context: Twenty-five thousand dollars a year, the presidential salary from 1789 until 1873.
facts.goDeeper: He saved most of it. His estate at his death was worth roughly $85,000, a considerable sum then.

facts.claim: Minutes Lincoln took to deliver the Gettysburg Address
facts.context: About two minutes, for roughly 270 words.
facts.goDeeper: The photographer at the scene was still setting up when Lincoln sat down. There is no confirmed photograph of him speaking.

facts.claim: Lincoln was the first president born outside the original thirteen states
facts.context: He was born in Kentucky, admitted to the Union in 1792. Every president before him was born in one of the original thirteen.
facts.goDeeper: His family moved to Indiana when he was seven, and to Illinois when he was twenty-one.

facts.claim: Lincoln had almost no formal schooling and taught himself law
facts.context: By his own estimate his formal education totalled under a year. He read law on his own and was admitted to the bar in 1836.
facts.goDeeper: He went on to argue more than 300 cases before the Illinois Supreme Court.

facts.claim: Lincoln was an accomplished wrestler as a young man
facts.context: He wrestled in his New Salem years and is honoured in the National Wrestling Hall of Fame.
facts.goDeeper: His most famous bout, against the local champion Jack Armstrong, is more legend than record, but the reputation was real.

facts.claim: Lincoln was the first American president to be assassinated
facts.context: Shot April 14, 1865. Three more presidents were later assassinated in office: Garfield, McKinley and Kennedy.
facts.goDeeper: An earlier attempt had been made on Andrew Jackson in 1835, when both of the attacker's pistols misfired.
